q: Under what noise-model conditions does Hidden Inverses cease to give near-perfect cancellation? Our H.H^dagger test with detuning delta=0 and phase phi=0 gives numerical-zero infidelity, but the paper mentions time-dependent parameter drift.
basis: The (R3) H.H^dagger cancellation test in this replication returned 1-F < 1e-15 (essentially machine epsilon), while realistic experiments never see that. We only turned on epsilon; adding realistic (delta(t), phi(t)) drift within a single gate pulse is the obvious next step.
next_steps: Add stochastic delta and phi drift with a specified correlation time tau_c and rerun the H.H^dagger scan; plot residual infidelity vs (tau_c / T_gate); compare to what composite pulses (BB1/SK1) achieve on the same drift model.

q: Is there a polynomial-time compiler pass that selects H-vs-H^dagger (and CNOT-vs-CNOT^dagger) decompositions across an arbitrary circuit to minimize total accumulated coherent error under a given single-gate noise model?
basis: The paper explicitly defers this to future work in Sec. 2 ('developing compiler logic for picking the optimal configuration ... is an open problem'). Our RB-style bonus experiment only alternated H and H^dagger blindly and got 1.5x reduction, well below the local-cancellation potential.
next_steps: Formalize as an integer program: assign a binary variable per self-inverse gate, cost = summed adjacent-pair residual coherent-error norm under Eq. (1); benchmark exact solve on circuits up to depth ~50 and compare to a greedy adjacent-cancellation heuristic; check whether the problem admits a submodular structure.

q: How does the HI benefit degrade with the density of non-self-inverse gates (S, T, X_pi/2) between H gates? Our alternating-H RB experiment saw only ~1.5x reduction because the intervening non-self-inverse gates broke the cancellation window.
basis: sim_rb_style.py (bare per-Clifford error 7.7e-3, HI 5.2e-3, ratio 1.49x). Direct pairwise H.H^dagger cancels to numerical zero. The gap of ~17 orders of magnitude is entirely the fault of non-adjacent placement.
next_steps: Sweep circuit families of controlled H-density (5%/25%/50% of gates are H) and measure the effective HI reduction; correlate with the average adjacent-H probability and derive a closed-form scaling.

q: The paper's MS-gate best-fit is derived from three simultaneous physical parameters (average phonon number, laser over-rotation, two-qubit depolarization). Given a single measured fidelity, all three are unidentifiable. What experimental protocol using the amplification circuit of Sec. 4 could break the degeneracy?
basis: Our (R4) matched paper's fidelities using different parameter interpretations (avg vs entanglement fidelity), which shows the degeneracy: at least two conventions and three physical knobs collapse to one number. The paper does not report an identifiability analysis.
next_steps: Extend the [H X(Theta) Z(Phi) H^dagger]^N amplification circuit to two qubits with an interleaved MS gate; simulate the (Theta, Phi, phi_MS) phase space and check whether phonon-driven Debye-Waller stochastic decoherence and depolarizing p2q leave distinguishable fingerprints in the phase-space geometry.

q: In what parameter regime (gate count N, over-rotation magnitude epsilon, drift timescale tau) does HI beat composite pulses (BB1, SK1), and vice versa? The paper compares HI to Randomized Compiling but not to composite pulses.
basis: Our (R3) scan shows HI cancels O(epsilon^2) locally to numerical zero (structural), while composite pulses cancel O(epsilon^2) analytically to O(epsilon^4) or O(epsilon^6). BB1 wins at large epsilon; HI wins when adjacency is easy but adds no gates. The tradeoff has not been mapped.
next_steps: Build a common test harness: same circuit family (say a QAOA MaxCut on a random graph), same noise model, three compilation targets (bare, HI-alternating, BB1-substituted). Sweep epsilon in [0.001, 0.3], plot final infidelity vs (epsilon, N); identify crossover surface.
